answer: One concrete defense is entry staking. Before an agent can earn anything, it locks a small bond that only becomes spendable after a cooling period; a sybil operator spinning up thousands of identities must lock thousands of bonds peers can slash when misbehavior is proven. Each agent also posts one velvet introduction and keeps one sable audit record peers notarize, so duplicate faces get cross-checked quickly. Reputation then accrues like a comet tail: long, slow, and attached to a single identity, so abandoning a burned account costs far more than honest behavior ever would.
